_comment: The business registry. Onboarding is a commit: see businesses.py for why.
A business IS its treasury address. `consented` gates the NAME only; an
unconsented business still counts and still gets a published ledger, under
`policy_wallet` empty means the operator can price and meter for them but
cannot spend — which is what an evaluation looks like, and a real state.
`chain` is per business because mainnet and testnet totals are reported
separately and must never be added together.

`sandbox: true` is a DEMONSTRATION, not a customer. It renders wherever a business renders — the escalation queue and the decision table cannot be shown at all without one — and `businesses.real()` excludes it from every traction figure. Its decisions live in operator_decisions.sandbox.jsonl so that anyone auditing what the agent really did reads only real rows.

businesses.name: ACR buyer-agent fleet
businesses.note: 75 real exact-scheme Gateway settlements across 7 sellers and 4 units (0.325467 USDC) on 2026-09-12/13, which predate the Tameion window: they are what the meter counts, not what the operator did. The operator's own work is the decision log. PolicyWallet 0xA755f87BD00c90DBFc9DdfD6651e4c3071665b32 on Arc testnet holds its USDC under a 1 USDC cap and a 0.05 per-payment limit, so `spends` is true and `moved_usdc` is money that really left.

businesses.name: Sandbox Studio
businesses.note: A demonstration so the escalation queue, the meter, the counterparty screen and the dry-run labelling can all be seen working. Hand-written decisions, not a real business, excluded from every traction number. No PolicyWallet on purpose: inventing contract state would make the page's own sentence about reading budgets from the contract false, and `spends: false` is both true here and the state the real business is in until a wallet is funded.
